a: two target-locale branches over one source persist and reload different policy, Wiki, drafts, costs, and patch histories without crossing identities.
m: A project binds account, engine/profile, source/build roots, source revision, source and target locales, work manifest, scope, and independently versioned locale branches.

a: adding a second target locale reuses source extraction and source Wiki while producing a disjoint localized bible, run, cost, and patch revision.
m: One source project can support several target languages without cloning or conflating source facts.

a: each selectable scope changes the exact required-unit set, and a surface outside the adapter’s target policy is rejected rather than silently skipped.
m: Translation scope is explicit across dialogue, speakers, choices, UI, images, and other adapter-supported surfaces.

a: a run receipt binds one exact policy version and a policy edit invalidates only dependent outputs.
m: Tone, honorifics, profanity, romanization, protected-span handling, ruby, punctuation, name treatment, and other locale policy are versioned per branch.

a: a changed active style rule changes the next affected draft or finding and leaves unrelated units memoized.
m: Abstract and granular style rules are persistent, evidence-backed, versioned artifacts consumed by drafting, editing, and review.

a: exact and inflected occurrences resolve the expected scoped term, while incompatible active terms produce a conflict rather than nondeterministic selection.
m: Canonical terms, variants, translations, do-not-translate forms, rationale, provenance, scope, and conflicts are governed as versioned data.

a: two concurrent attempts to add the same scoped surface form result in one canonical term and one typed duplicate outcome.
m: New terminology candidates are checked transactionally against the active repository vocabulary before insertion or use.

a: an authorized query returns ranked branch-compatible matches and an unauthorized query cannot recover target text or source identifiers.
m: Accepted and historical source-target units are searchable by exact, normalized, contextual, and fuzzy evidence without leaking private text to unauthorized reads.

a: changing one source unit invalidates its dependent targets and refuses a stale patch while preserving unrelated accepted work.
m: Every context item, model output, finding, correction, patch, and runtime observation binds the source unit and revision it was derived from.

a: a unit selected from two different engines receives graph-derived context through the same interface and every claimed link resolves to native evidence.
m: Engine structure, route, scene, choice, speaker, predecessor, successor, and asset links become a common localization graph.

a: two works share a canonical character fact but apply different scoped voice rules, and the drafting receipt identifies both sources.
m: Works carved from one archive inherit shared brand/super-scope facts and maintain work-specific glossary, character, style, route, and entry-point overrides.

a: editing a target policy cannot mutate the source Wiki snapshot, and a source-evidence correction invalidates every dependent locale branch.
m: Source facts remain immutable evidence while target-language interpretations, names, style, and adaptation are locale-specific.

a: every physical invocation resolves exactly one active profile and an absent, uncertified, or incompatible profile pauses before network egress.
m: Each role resolves an approved model, provider posture, prompt/schema version, context/output limits, retry policy, and certification from data.

a: a run manifest records the selected profile per role and changing one role’s profile invalidates only that role’s dependent steps.
m: Different analysis, production, repair, and review roles can use independently certified model profiles rather than one global model.

a: the certificate verifies against the provider artifact and generation identity, while fabricated, replay-substituted, expired, or differently served evidence fails validation.
m: A model profile is certified from a real provider generation binding exact model, served provider, wire mode, schema, limits, privacy posture, and evaluation evidence rather than a self-signed checksum.

a: a call-site audit finds no production network path around the primitive, and injected failures have the same typed semantics across every role.
m: All model calls traverse one auditable dispatch primitive that owns request formation, structured-output mode, identity, timeouts, cancellation, usage, privacy, and errors.

a: a production run with no live provider configuration pauses or fails before drafting, and a guard rejects fake-provider construction on every production command route.
m: Production localization and semantic-agent entrypoints cannot silently select fixture, denial, recorded, or fake providers.

a: a bounded live call records the served pair and ZDR evidence; an unapproved served pair quarantines the response and cannot feed an accepted output.
m: Provider/model pairs are admitted only when current account and route evidence satisfy the declared zero-data-retention posture.

a: provider-side fallback yields a distinct served pair in the ledger and cost dashboard, and missing or contradictory identity makes the call unverified.
m: Requested and actually served model/provider identity, generation ID, fallback decision, and capability posture are retained per physical call.

a: each admitted pair has a current successful probe for its selected wire mode and an unsupported mode is removed or routed through an explicitly validated alternative.
m: Structured-output and privacy modes are probed against the permitted provider set rather than assumed from stale model metadata.

a: each mode is used only after a successful live probe, a route incapable of both structured modes follows the explicitly selected third policy, and stale capability data fails closed.
m: Schema, JSON-object, and any permitted plain-completion mode are selected from measured capabilities of the admitted served-pair route.

a: extra fields, wrong types, foreign unit IDs, invalid spans, prose wrappers, and truncated JSON all fail before persistence as accepted output.
m: Every role output is validated against its exact schema, field semantics, unit scope, protected spans, and bounds before use.

a: malformed output either becomes schema-valid through the configured permitted mechanism or exhausts into a resumable operational pause, with every attempt retained and billed.
m: Mechanical output failures follow one bounded, observable recovery policy with retry accounting and no semantic fabrication.

a: injecting transient, malformed, timeout, cancellation, budget, and permanent failures into each phase yields the same classified state transition.
m: Every model phase shares retry, backoff, deadline, cancellation, schema validation, spend admission, and pause/resume semantics.

a: serial and concurrent runs produce equivalent accepted outputs and lineage, and a race probe cannot contaminate one unit with another unit’s evidence.
m: Whole-project execution supports validated concurrency while isolating per-unit context, attempts, speaker labels, and outputs.

a: no emitted batch exceeds any declared cap when recomputed from its complete payload, and repeated planning yields the same membership.
m: Compatible units can be packed under model context, output, per-item card, and budget caps with deterministic membership and tail handling.

a: concurrent identical requests make one billed provider call, later replay makes zero calls, and changing any meaningful input creates a new key.
m: Every provider-visible physical step is content-addressed, memoized, and singleflighted by its full deterministic input.

a: a late response after cancellation or a mismatched generation ID is persisted as evidence but never changes an accepted checkpoint.
m: Unverified, incomplete, mismatched, cancelled, or superseded provider responses remain quarantined until identity, schema, usage, and dependency checks pass.

a: replay reconstructs the exact state from events, no accepted record is overwritten, and the public lineage contains hashes/counts/classes rather than private text.
m: Calls, attempts, events, outputs, feedback, and Wiki changes are append-only and content-free where exposed publicly.

a: every accepted patch unit traces to exact fact, prompt, call, output, and review nodes, and an orphan or cycle is rejected.
m: Dependency-linked outputs form a transcript DAG with immutable snapshots and explicitly accepted heads.

a: two competing publishers yield one accepted head and one retryable conflict without losing either immutable event.
m: Concurrent workers publish run and project snapshots through compare-and-swap heads rather than last-writer wins.

a: a fault injected at every enumerated boundary resumes to one accepted outcome with no duplicate bill, lost attempt, or falsely terminal run.
m: Runs recover correctly when the process dies before request, during request, after response, during validation, persistence, checkpointing, patch export, or finalization.

a: concurrent workers cannot both commit one leased step, stale workers are fenced, and crash recovery preserves every completed attempt and exact spend.
m: The journal-era refinement graph was retired because content-addressed workflow artifacts replaced its attempt, reservation, lease, fence, checkpoint, and terminalization model.

a: all valid transitions succeed once, every invalid or stale transition fails, and no run reports success with failed required units.
m: Pending, running, pausing, paused, resuming, completed, failed, and cancelled states have exact allowed transitions and one terminal summary.

a: aggregate totals exactly equal underlying unique work items under concurrency and cannot count retries as additional units.
m: Progress records planned, active, retrying, paused, accepted, and failed work per unit and role with aggregate project views.

a: two projects execute at once, pausing or cancelling one leaves the other’s state and spend unchanged, and portfolio totals reconcile.
m: Several projects and locale branches can run concurrently with isolated leases/checkpoints, progress, budgets, and costs.

a: every stored token value is traceable to a provider response; an absent token field remains unknown and cannot become zero or a heuristic count.
m: Successful calls retain provider-reported input, output, cached, reasoning, and other token dimensions without estimating absent values.

a: run, project, role, pair, and dashboard aggregates all equal the provider artifacts to exact decimal precision, and missing billed cost fails any path that requires a cost-complete result.
m: Cost accounting uses provider-billed values at full precision per actual served pair and attempt, including retries and enrichments.

a: independently recomputed aggregates equal stored read models, and two providers serving one model remain separate.
m: Invocation counts, token dimensions, latency, cache behavior, errors, and billed cost are queryable per project, run, role, step, requested pair, and served pair.

a: concurrent reservations cannot overspend, unused reservations release on every outcome, confirmed cost survives resume, and cap exhaustion invokes no fallback model.
m: Atomic spend admission prevents projected or confirmed spend from crossing a configured cap and pauses resumably rather than silently downgrading.

a: planted private payloads never enter unauthorized logs, public reports, or disallowed providers, while an authorized private run retains the evidence its policy permits.
m: Prompts, responses, Wiki facts, local paths, source text, retention, caching, web search, provider metadata, and artifacts obey a declared private/public and egress policy.

a: arbitrary nested secrets, paths, raw responses, and personal data added to provider metadata are absent from every serialized public or dashboard object.
m: Provider metadata crosses persistence and public boundaries only through an allowlisted typed projection, never verbatim pass-through.

a: generated character/markup cases produce zero TypeScript/Rust disagreement and an unencodable target fails before patchback rather than during it.
m: Model-facing normalization and adapter patch validation agree exactly on representability, normalization, byte length, and protected syntax for the selected engine policy.

a: the same source revision produces the same snapshot hash, while any fact or structure edit creates a new hash and precisely identifies affected descendants.
m: A deterministic pre-pass freezes the exact source facts, structure, unit inventory, asset evidence, and dependency graph used by a run.

a: every tool call returns a strict shape with provenance and caps, and arbitrary filesystem, SQL, cross-project, or unbounded reads are denied.
m: Agents can query only bounded, typed, revision-bound local tools for units, structure, Wiki, glossary, assets, and prior accepted outputs.

a: all other roles are technically unable to browse, and imported research contains no private source text or unsupported claim.
m: External research is limited to the designated research role, occurs outside private/ZDR prompt context, and persists only validated claims and citations.

a: every configured object kind validates, links through stable IDs, and rejects unknown fields, dangling dependencies, or unproven claims.
m: Characters, relationships, places, organizations, terms, routes, scenes, events, items, systems, themes, style, and other facts use strict versioned Wiki objects.

a: every factual field can navigate to source unit, structure evidence, asset, or permitted external citation, and an unsupported factual value fails claim validation.
m: Fine-grained Wiki fields carry claim status, evidence, navigable citations, confidence, conflicts, and dependencies.

a: identical media produces one hash identity, changed bytes invalidate dependent renderings, and public export cannot include a private media blob.
m: Images and other Wiki media are content-addressed, privacy-classified, linked to claims and source assets, and deduplicated.

a: every required object/field has a populated value or exact source-absent evidence, all dependencies resolve, and the completeness report can fail on one removed entry.
m: The orchestration cold-builds a complete source-language Wiki covering the configured project and work scopes before localization.

a: a shared entity resolves once across two works, an intentional per-work difference remains distinct, and provenance identifies its scope.
m: Shared universe or brand facts can be linked across works while work-local facts and contradictions remain scoped.

a: an edit creates a versioned claim change with actor/audit evidence and cannot mutate the prior snapshot.
m: Authorized playtesters can browse and edit canonical facts, style, glossary, character, and relationship knowledge through CLI and dashboard.

a: changing one character’s address term reruns dependent units and leaves an unrelated route entirely cache-hit.
m: Wiki edits invalidate only physical steps whose declared field/claim dependencies changed.

a: an optional enhancement produces a new dependent revision while the prior patch remains reproducible and visibly superseded, not erased.
m: Feedback and later enrichment can improve Wiki objects without blocking already complete configured-scope output unless a required ground-truth field is absent.

a: all mandatory fields are populated with source links and policy evidence before dependent drafting begins; removing one required field blocks that run at a resumable boundary.
m: Every target locale receives a complete localized rendering of required source Wiki facts, terminology, names, relationships, voice, and adaptation decisions.

a: prompts and output lineage cite the same bible version, and a target fact contradicting it is rejected or creates an explicit conflict.
m: Drafting, editing, QA, and repair must consume the accepted localized bible rather than invent independent context.

a: translation and every relevant QA role bind the same packet hash, and no unresolved reference or foreign-unit speaker label reaches a prompt.
m: Each unit receives a materialized, immutable packet containing exact scene, route, story-so-far, character, relationship, speaker, terminology, style, sibling, and cross-work evidence.

a: an accepted enrichment is visible to a later dependent unit and a rejected enrichment cannot alter canonical context.
m: Context construction both consumes existing facts and writes validated enrichment back through central persistence with dependency-aware invalidation.

a: malformed or uncitable enrichment is quarantined with telemetry, while the dependent run either proceeds from its declared deterministic minimum or pauses only if that artifact is explicitly required.
m: Optional model-generated summaries and relationship/route enrichments may fail without displacing deterministic decoded context or fabricating facts.

a: every role belongs to exactly one profile and a role cannot invoke a tool or emit an artifact outside its profile.
m: Analysis, production, and quality profiles define the allowed tools, context, output, model policy, and dependencies for their roles.

a: the run manifest schedules exactly the configured nineteen roles where policy requires them, and an added, omitted, or duplicate identity fails roster validation.
m: The workflow has an explicit nineteen-role manifest with stable identities and no hidden or dynamically invented production role.

a: its artifact populates every required style field with citations or source-absent evidence and contains no verbatim private dialogue.
m: The Style Lead derives persistent abstract prose, register, punctuation, presentation, and genre conventions without copying source dialogue.

a: seeded recurring terms produce deduplicated candidates with occurrence evidence, conflicts, and no unrelated capitalized-string guesses.
m: The Terminology Analyst discovers, reconciles, scopes, and proposes canonical terms and variants.

a: ordered scenes yield cumulative summaries that include prior established facts, exclude future-only facts, and cite their source units.
m: The Scene Analyst summarizes scene purpose, beats, state changes, dependencies, and progressive story-so-far.

a: a seeded contradiction is surfaced with both citations and never silently resolved without evidence.
m: The Continuity and Lore Reconciler finds cross-scene facts, contradictions, foreshadowing, callbacks, and canonical resolutions.

a: one character receives distinguishable evidence-backed voice guidance for two contexts and the downstream reviewer detects a seeded context swap.
m: The Granular Voice Director specifies character voice by relationship, audience, emotional state, route, and evolution rather than generic adjectives.

a: a seeded culture-bound item yields alternatives, rationale, protected meaning, and policy linkage rather than an untraceable rewrite.
m: The Cultural Adaptation Analyst proposes locale-appropriate handling of jokes, references, honorifics, wordplay, and sensitive material under branch policy.

a: required biography fields carry citations and a planted unsupported fact is rejected.
m: The Character Biographer builds evidence-backed identity, history, goals, traits, names, and optional permitted external research.

a: a relationship-changing event updates the correct directed edge and dependent speech guidance while preserving the prior version.
m: The Relationships and Background Analyst models directed relationships, history, address forms, power, intimacy, and changes over time.

a: two routes produce distinct ordered arcs linked to branch evidence and do not leak future or alternate-route facts into earlier context.
m: The Character-in-Route Arc Analyst tracks each character’s route-specific states, beats, motivations, and divergence from shared context.

a: a seeded ambiguous line resolves only when the supporting evidence is available, and unresolved cases remain explicit rather than defaulting to “unknown” or a guess.
m: The Hindsight Speaker Resolver uses later and sibling evidence to resolve ambiguous speaker identity while preserving reveal timing and uncertainty.

a: every in-scope unit receives one nonblank aligned draft, the scene reads coherently in order, and no unit is dropped, merged, or source-echoed.
m: The Whole-Scene Localizer writes a coherent target scene from the complete scoped unit set and localized bible, preserving unit alignment and protected structure.

a: edits remain semantically aligned and span-safe, and a seeded awkward line improves without changing its factual proposition.
m: The Line Editor improves fluency, pacing, consistency, and presentation while respecting scene intent, policy, and unit constraints.

a: each repair references a finding, changes only dependent fields or units, and clears the targeted deterministic check.
m: The Semantic Repair role corrects specific evidenced meaning, structure, terminology, and constraint failures without rewriting unaffected content.

a: a calibrated set of seeded meaning defects is detected with unit and evidence references, while clean controls remain within the frozen false-positive bound.
m: The Meaning Reviewer identifies omissions, additions, mistranslations, referents, polarity, modality, and factual shifts.

a: a seeded voice swap is found and classified at the correct context scope without penalizing an intentional documented variation.
m: The Voice Reviewer checks character-, relationship-, scene-, and arc-specific voice against the localized bible.

a: every seeded term violation is found, approved variants pass, and findings point to the governing term version.
m: The Terminology Auditor checks glossary usage, variants, capitalization, name forms, and protected terms.

a: a seeded cross-scene contradiction is found with both citations and unrelated alternate-route knowledge is not introduced.
m: The Continuity Reviewer checks chronology, facts, callbacks, route scope, relationship state, and spoiler discipline.

a: replaying the real patched output finds seeded overflow, tofu, wrong branch label, and missing image text with frame/moment evidence.
m: The Build-LQA Reviewer evaluates patched-byte runtime presentation, boxes, glyphs, wrapping, choices, images, and interactive behavior.

a: a disagreement fixture yields a reproducible disposition citing both reviews and governing evidence, with no unsupported majority shortcut.
m: The Adjudicator reconciles reviewer disagreements against frozen evidence and policy into findings or targeted repair instructions.

a: every accepted patch unit has a complete lineage path through required stages, and removing any required artifact prevents terminal success.
m: The product executes a declared dependency graph from source facts and Wiki through bible, analysis, whole-scene drafting, editing, review, repair, accepted outputs, patch, replay, and feedback.

a: each mode’s execution matches its manifest and a replay-only run makes zero model calls.
m: Cold build, incremental refinement, feedback iteration, replay-only, and pure-MTL ablation modes declare exact context, output, roster, model-call, and reuse behavior.

a: random valid scheduling produces the same accepted DAG, and a role cannot start with a missing dependency.
m: Roles run when their declared immutable inputs are accepted, allowing safe parallelism without hidden temporal coupling.

a: a multi-unit scene is translated as one planned artifact and re-materializes exactly one target per required bridge unit.
m: Production translation operates on coherent scene context while retaining one-to-one bridge-unit targets needed for patchback.

a: terminal success reports required count equal to unique written-target count and fails when any target is absent, blank, duplicated, or normalized-identical source echo under a translation-required policy.
m: Every in-scope unit ends with exactly one best-effort, nonblank written target; QA annotates quality but cannot replace it with blank, source echo, or deferral.

a: seeded parenthetical notes and prose wrappers are detected and excluded or repaired before an output can enter patchback.
m: Delivered target fields contain only localized game text, never translator notes, explanations, markdown, refusal prose, or model meta-commentary.

a: a run with one unresolved quality finding but complete valid targets can produce a versioned patch under the non-gating model, while one missing unit cannot.
m: Run completion is governed by complete configured-scope written coverage and mechanical patch validity, with quality findings retained separately.

a: one mutation in each rule fails at its owning boundary with no provider judgment needed.
m: Source hashes, unit coverage, encoding, protected spans, terminology invariants, target scope, patchability, and schema integrity are checked deterministically before outputs advance.

a: every finding resolves to an in-scope output and source/bible evidence; a foreign or unscorable unit cannot inflate or suppress quality totals.
m: Reviewers emit typed, scored, calibrated findings with unit, field, evidence, rationale, and suggested repair rather than hidden pass/fail booleans.

a: a seeded failure is repaired and passes its check, while unrelated unit and artifact hashes remain unchanged.
m: Repair plans compose applicable findings into bounded edits, revalidate deterministic constraints, and preserve unaffected accepted work.

a: the selected policy is present in the run manifest and the evidence chain shows exactly the required post-repair steps; the ledger does not settle which policy is canonical.
m: The workflow explicitly records whether repaired drafts receive only deterministic checks or a second semantic QA pass.

a: resolving the blocker resumes the same run and unit identities with no lost accepted work or invented draft.
m: Provider, budget, credential, infrastructure, and missing-required-bible blockers pause the run at a resumable boundary rather than creating source echoes or per-unit human deferrals.

a: pass N+1 traces to pass N feedback and changed dependencies, and a reported successful pass cannot contain failed required rerun units.
m: Iterative passes record input patch/version, feedback, changed facts/policy, rerun scope, outputs, costs, and successor relationship.

a: two iterations remain independently reproducible and the newer version’s diff links every change to feedback or invalidated knowledge.
m: Each run yields one immutable patch version; later playtest feedback creates a new refinement run and version rather than mutating delivery history.

a: editing one target creates a new accepted output and patch revision, preserves the old version, and replay observes the new text.
m: A target-language result editor can commit line or scene revisions directly into a new delivered patch version without an approval gate.

a: a context edit identifies the exact invalidation set, a real worker reruns it, and the next draft changes while unrelated units remain cached.
m: Feedback can correct canonical Wiki, glossary, style, speaker, or relationship context and schedule registered dependent reruns.

a: valid feedback produces a versioned event and invalid/stale/unauthorized feedback creates no partial side effects.
m: Individual or batched playtest annotations retain actor, target, category, frame/moment/unit links, private/public class, and intended correction scope.

a: authorized transitions apply atomically to real DB records, stale or denied actions fail distinctly, and queue summaries reconcile to item state.
m: The alternate per-unit reviewer queue was retired because it deferred durable localization and duplicated the canonical result, context, Wiki, and iteration path.

a: an accepted asset decision produces the expected changed asset in a patch, while a rejected or stale decision produces no write.
m: Image/OCR and other non-text localization candidates can carry decisions, target assets, patchability, evidence, and revision history.

a: the ablation completes with its reduced-context manifest, exact real cost, and no access to Wiki or agent outputs prohibited by the mode.
m: A context-minimal machine-translation baseline uses the same source units, provider accounting, patching, and evaluation interfaces for fair comparison.

a: a qualifying run enters the benchmark with source split and cost linkage, while absent cost or replay consent fails closed.
m: Accepted localization runs can be converted into blind benchmark contestants only with explicit replay intent, provenance, and complete recorded cost.

a: a large project completes with unique input/output counts, bounded concurrency, exact costs, and no hand-authored per-unit invocation.
m: A generic executor runs every configured project/work unit through context, drafting, QA, repair, persistence, patch export, replay, and summary.

a: projects from three engine families traverse one workflow; adding the third requires adapter registration, not orchestration edits.
m: The localization workflow consumes discriminated bridge, structure, target-policy, patchback, and runtime interfaces rather than assuming RealLive or another family.

a: one command or API run produces linked artifacts for every leg from real source bytes to visible translated pixels, and substituting a fixture sentinel fails the receipt.
m: A single product composition joins real extraction, Wiki/context, live model calls, accepted targets, patchback, delta/export, replay, and rendered evidence.

a: a fresh non-developer installation completes the declared vertical through these commands and no command requires a title-specific script or manual bridge conversion.
m: User-shaped `extract`, `structure-export`, `localize`, `localize-game`, `patch`, and `validate` commands expose the generic workflow with strict configs and diagnostics.

a: equivalent requests through CLI and HTTP yield the same run identity, validation outcome, and artifact contract.
m: CLI, HTTP, jobs, and Studio actions delegate to one workflow composition rather than duplicating provider, persistence, or engine logic.

a: a representative tens-of-thousands-unit run completes or pauses/resumes under declared limits with exact unique-unit accounting and no single-row or per-unit serial bottleneck.
m: The executor, persistence, batching, progress, cost, and recovery paths are intended to operate at whole-game unit counts rather than toy scenes.

a: seeded failures in every class produce the intended category and a message containing another category’s token cannot change classification.
m: End-to-end failures distinguish in-profile product bugs, out-of-profile limitations, operational pauses, content findings, and invalid inputs from evidence rather than stderr substring matching.

a: replay makes zero provider calls, reproduces accepted artifacts and aggregates, and fails if any lineage dependency or score input is absent.
m: A completed run emits a strict quality/privacy/cost/coverage scorecard and can be reconstructed without further model calls.
